summary: Describes using X.25 to carry PPP-encapsulated packets, so multi-protocol traffic can run over an X.25 connection. It is a standards-track proposal.

eli5.summary: PPP is a way to send different kinds of messages down one line. This explains how to do it over an older phone-company-style network.

subtitle: How to use X.25 virtual circuits as the framing layer for PPP, and how a call announces it.

tldr.problem: PPP needs a framing layer, and some point-to-point links are provided over X.25 equipment rather than plain HDLC lines.
tldr.mechanism: PPP uses the X.25 frame header in place of the HDLC header and ignores other X.25 features. On switched circuits, the first octet of Call User Data carries the PPP NLPID, CF hex, to signal PPP.
tldr.outcome: A Proposed Standard that lets PPP, with its LCP, NCPs, authentication and compression, run over X.25 point-to-point circuits.

facts.label: Network layer MTU
facts.value: No more than 1500 unless peer MRU is 2048 or greater

today: RFC 1598 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Run PPP in X.25
sections.content:
CCITT recommendation X.25 describes a network layer protocol that offers error-free, sequenced, flow controlled virtual circuits. Its data link layer, X.25 LAPB, builds on ISO 3309, 4335 and 6256. PPP's own HDLC framing is also based on ISO 3309.

When X.25 is set up as a point-to-point circuit, PPP can use it purely as a framing mechanism and ignore its other features. The RFC compares this to the technique used to carry SNAP headers over X.25.

The memo applies only to point-to-point links. Its Applicability note says PPP facilities such as LCP, network-layer control protocols, authentication and compression need a point-to-point relationship and are not designed for multi-point or multi-access environments.

The authors once hoped PPP HDLC frames and X.25 frames could share a link while equipment was converted gradually. Some switches strip the X.25 header, carry the packets over something like Frame Relay, and rebuild the header at the last hop, so co-existence and gradual migration are ruled out.
sections.eli5: X.25 is an old network that already knows how to move envelopes safely. PPP just borrows its envelope and ignores the rest of what X.25 can do.

sections.title: Physical Layer Requirements
sections.content:
PPP treats X.25 framing as a bit synchronous link. The link MUST be full-duplex, and may be dedicated (permanent) or switched. PPP presents an octet interface to the physical layer and imposes no transmission rate limit beyond that of the particular X.25 interface.

X.25 needs control signals that show when the link is connected or disconnected, and these supply the Up and Down events to the LCP state machine. PPP does not normally need control signals, so their failure MUST NOT affect correct operation of PPP. Encodings are the job of the DTE/DCE equipment and outside this specification, though X.25 requires NRZ encoding.
sections.eli5: The wire has to carry talk in both directions at once. If the little lights that say the line is connected fail, PPP must keep working anyway.

sections.title: The Frame Format
sections.content:
Because both PPP in HDLC framing and X.25 are based on ISO 3309, the X.25 header is simply substituted for the smaller HDLC header. The frame follows the principles and terminology of RFC 1356, which this memo summarizes rather than repeats. It starts with a flag of 0x7e, then Address and Control octets, the D and Q bits with a 12-bit SVC number split into high and low parts, the p(r), M and p(s) fields and a zero bit, and then the PPP Protocol field. The PPP Protocol, Information and Padding fields are as described in the PPP encapsulation specification.

LCP can negotiate changes to the basic frame, but modified frames are always clearly distinguishable from standard ones. Two rules apply. Address-and-Control-Field-Compression MUST NOT be negotiated, since the Address and Control values are not constant and are changed as the frame crosses the network. Protocol-Field-Compression SHOULD be negotiated when it improves throughput: X.25 framing does not align the Information field on a 32-bit boundary, but it reaches 16-bit alignment when the Protocol field is compressed to one octet.
sections.eli5: Each PPP message gets an X.25 address label on the front. Because the network keeps rewriting parts of that label, the two ends must not try to shorten those parts.

sections.title: Call Setup and the PPP NLPID
sections.content:
On a Permanent Virtual Circuit (PVC), SVC call setup and clearing is not required, and calls are established and terminated with PPP LCP packets.

On a Switched Virtual Circuit (SVC), the first octet of the Call User Data (CUD) field in the Call Request packet selects the protocol, following the Subsequent Protocol Identifier in ISO/IEC TR 9577. That octet is a Network Layer Protocol Identifier (NLPID). PPP is indicated by the NLPID value CF hex, and any later octets in the CUD are extraneous and MUST be ignored.

  • Multipoint networks (or multicast groups) MUST refuse calls that carry the PPP NLPID.
  • Accidentally connecting a link to a multipoint network SHOULD cause a misconfiguration indication, which can be detected as multiple responses to one LCP Configure-Request Identifier from different framing addresses.
  • Conformance requires support for the PPP NLPID (CF). Conformance with RFC 1356 also requires the IP NLPID (CC), and does not require others such as Zero (00), SNAP (80), CLNP (81) or ES-IS (82).
  • When IP address negotiation or VJ header compression is wanted, PPP call setup SHOULD be tried first. If it fails, the normal IP call setup MUST be used.

The PPP NLPID SHOULD NOT be used to sort circuits that use the Zero NLPID. If such a circuit coexists with PPP circuits, only network layer traffic not negotiated by the associated NCP goes over the Zero NLPID circuit.

Rationale in the RFC: failed calls are usually free, so probing for PPP with a call is cheap. Probing with PPP configuration packets on every Zero NLPID call could cost money when users pay per packet or connect time. PPP configuration also gives a direct indication of service, avoiding the "black-holes" of the Zero NLPID technique.
sections.eli5: When you phone a switched circuit, you say in the first byte what language you will speak. PPP has its own secret number, CF. If the other side does not speak PPP, you just hang up and use the ordinary way.

sections.title: Configuration Details
sections.content:
The recommended Configuration Options are Magic Number and Protocol Field Compression. The standard LCP defaults apply to X.25 links, except for the MRU.

To interoperate with existing X.25 implementations, the initial Maximum-Receive-Unit (MRU) is 1600 octets. This only sets the minimum buffer space for receiving and does not limit the size of packets sent. A typical feeding network has an MRU of either 1500, or 2048 or greater, so the network layer MTU SHOULD NOT exceed 1500 unless a peer MRU of 2048 or greater is specifically negotiated, to avoid fragmentation.

X.25 packet size is not directly tied to the MRU. PDUs are sent as X.25 complete packet sequences: each PDU begins on an X.25 data packet boundary, and the M bit (more data) fragments PDUs that are longer than one data packet.
sections.eli5: The envelope starts out able to hold 1600 bytes of letter, but you should send letters of at most 1500 so nothing has to be cut up on the way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Implementations MUST NOT assume that PPP authentication done at call setup for one circuit between two systems also covers concurrent circuits between the same two systems. Over-relying on the integrity and security of switching systems and administrations leaves possible gaps, and an insertion attack might go undetected. An attacker able to spoof the same calling identity might avoid link authentication.
sections.eli5: Showing your ID once on one phone call does not prove who is on a different call. Each call has to prove itself.
